agent_summary:
Target juice.lab.test answers only on HTTP (port 443 refused); it is OWASP Juice Shop v20.2.0 (Angular SPA + Express/REST, nginx front). All 13 WSTG-CLNT items were worked read-only.

Key client-side findings (leads recorded):
- WSTG-CLNT-04 Open redirect (DONE/lead, medium): /redirect?to= only substring-whitelists targets, bypassable via /redirect?to=https://evil.example.com/?pwn=<whitelisted> → 302 to attacker host.
- WSTG-CLNT-13 XSSI/JSONP (DONE/lead, medium): /rest/user/whoami?callback=foo returns text/javascript JSONP wrapping session data; the callback name is stripped of non-alphanumerics (no callback-name XSS) but the JSONP+ACAO:* allows cross-origin inclusion to read authenticated whoami data.
- WSTG-CLNT-01/02/03 DOM XSS / JS exec / HTML injection (DONE/lead, high on DOM XSS): server does not encode the reflected search q and returns raw HTML in API fields (product descriptions, welcomeBanner) that the SPA renders via bypassSecurityTrustHtml/innerHTML — the classic #/search?q DOM-XSS sink; actual execution needs a browser to confirm (flagged for human validation).
- WSTG-CLNT-07 CORS (DONE): REST uses a static Access-Control-Allow-Origin:* (never reflects Origin, no Allow-Credentials); preflight reflects requested Allow-Headers; socket.io restricts to http://localhost:4200. Wildcard without credentials, so not a credentialed-data leak.
- WSTG-CLNT-09 Clickjacking (DONE): X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN on all responses, no CSP frame-ancestors — cross-origin framing blocked by XFO.
- WSTG-CLNT-10 WebSockets (DONE): Socket.IO handshake at /socket.io/ confirmed, origin limited to localhost:4200.
- WSTG-CLNT-05 CSS injection (DONE): styles.css is standard Angular Material, theme from server config; no user-controlled CSS sink beyond the HTML-render path.
- WSTG-CLNT-06 Client-side resource manipulation (DONE): demonstrated via the attacker-controlled /redirect target.
- WSTG-CLNT-11 Web messaging (DONE): app messaging is Socket.IO; no insecure window.postMessage handler surfaced in the reviewed bundles (runtime confirmation needs a browser).
- WSTG-CLNT-12 Browser storage (DONE/lead, medium): bundle handles a JWT auth token that Juice Shop stores in localStorage/cookie, readable by any XSS (browser needed to inspect contents).
- WSTG-CLNT-08 Cross-site flashing (N/A): no Flash/SWF content.

Out-of-lane leads also recorded for the reviewer/other lanes: unauthenticated data exposure via /rest/memories (user emails + password hashes), /metrics, /ftp directory listing and /encryptionkeys & /support/logs listings; poison-null-byte extension-filter bypass (/ftp/package.json.bak%2500.md serves the restricted .bak); verbose Express stack traces on errors; security-question/user enumeration via /rest/user/security-question.

Surface coverage: enumerated the SPA bundle routes and server paths, fetched index.html, all main JS chunks/modules, styles.css, i18n, and exercised REST models (/api/* and /rest/*). Protected endpoints (api/Users, Cards, Addresss, BasketItems, SecurityAnswers, wallet, order-history, basket) correctly returned 401; unknown paths fall through to the SPA index (catch-all). Reachable unauthenticated endpoints are named above. No writes were attempted (engagement is read-only); DOM-XSS execution, postMessage listeners and localStorage contents remain the only items needing a browser to fully confirm.

leads.title: [agent] DOM-based XSS sink in client-side search rendering (#/search?q=)

detail.text: The search endpoint accepts and reflects arbitrary markup in q without server-side encoding, and the SPA renders the search term/product HTML via Angular's bypassSecurityTrustHtml (innerHTML). This matches the well-known Juice Shop DOM XSS; a browser-based check of #/search?q=<iframe src="javascript:alert(document.domain)"> should confirm execution. Needs human/browser validation.

GET /encryptionkeys returns 200 HTML (7954 bytes) and GET /support/logs returns 200 HTML (8922 bytes), both browsable directory listings served without authentication. These expose cryptographic key files and application log files respectively. Server-side information disclosure for the relevant lane/reviewer.

leads.title: [agent] JSONP/XSSI on /rest/user/whoami exposes authenticated user data cross-origin

detail.text: GET /rest/user/whoami?callback=foo responds with text/javascript "/**/ typeof foo === 'function' && foo({...})". This JSONP wrapper lets any external site include the endpoint as <script src> and read the victim's session-bound whoami response (user id/email when authenticated), bypassing same-origin protections. Cross-site script inclusion.

leads.title: [agent] JWT auth token stored in client-accessible browser storage

detail.text: Juice Shop stores the authentication JWT in localStorage (key 'token') and a non-HttpOnly cookie, as reflected by the client bundle's authToken handling. Combined with the DOM-XSS/HTML-injection sinks on this host, an XSS would be able to read the token and hijack the session. Confirm by inspecting localStorage in a browser after login.

leads.title: [agent] Open redirect in /redirect?to= via whitelist bypass

detail.text: GET /redirect?to=https://evil.example.com/?pwn=https://github.com/juice-shop/juice-shop returns HTTP 302 with Location: https://evil.example.com/?pwn=... The server-side whitelist (routes/redirect.js) only checks that a whitelisted URL appears as a substring, so appending it as a query parameter redirects users to an arbitrary external host. Reflected-redirect phishing vector.

leads.title: [agent] Poison null byte path/extension-filter bypass serves restricted /ftp backup files

detail.text: GET /ftp/package.json.bak returns 403 (extension not whitelisted), but GET /ftp/package.json.bak%2500.md (double-encoded null byte) returns 200 with the actual backup file content (application/octet-stream, 4263 bytes; a jsonwebtoken value was present). The /ftp static handler's extension allowlist (.md/.pdf) is bypassable with a poison null byte, exposing .bak/.yml/.kdbx files such as package.json.bak and suspicious_errors.yml. Server-side file-access issue for the relevant lane/reviewer.

leads.title: [agent] Unauthenticated data exposure via /rest/memories, /metrics and /ftp directory listing

detail.text: GET /rest/memories (no auth) returns all memory records including embedded User objects with email, password hash, deluxeToken and role for multiple users. GET /metrics exposes Prometheus process/runtime metrics unauthenticated. GET /ftp returns a browsable directory listing (acquisitions.md, package.json.bak, incident-support.kdbx, coupons_2013.md.bak, etc.). Also the /redirect error page leaks full server stack traces with source file paths. These are server-side/data-exposure issues for the relevant lane/reviewer.
